h: A heist crew breaks into people's dreams to plant an idea, and the rules of each dream layer keep tightening the clock.

like.r: Another dream-invasion thriller where the boundary between sleeping and waking collapses, more surreal and far less tidy.

like.t: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
like.r: Also set inside a mind, but its memory-maze is about a breakup rather than a heist and hurts more.
The director's earlier puzzle about memory and self-deception, smaller, scrappier and told backwards.

h: A broken Batman returns to a Gotham on the brink of revolt for the closing chapter of Nolan's trilogy; huge, grim and operatic.

like.r: Another masked figure inciting a city against an authoritarian state, with a cheekier, more ideological bent.
The crime epic that shaped Nolan's city-scale tension, with cops and thieves rather than a masked vigilante.
The revolutionary-mob backdrop and sacrificial ending of the film come straight from this novel.

h: Astronauts leave a dying Earth through a wormhole while a daughter waits at home; science spectacle that wants you to cry.

like.r: The cosmic-scale ancestor of this film, colder and more enigmatic where Nolan reaches for feeling.
Another scientist chasing answers beyond the stars, with faith and a father-daughter bond at its center.
Also rigorous about physics, but light, funny and focused on one man solving problems.

h: The 1940 evacuation told as three interlocking clocks on land, sea and air, with almost no dialogue and relentless dread.

like.r: Immersive, visceral war filmmaking, but built around a mission and characters you come to know.
Another war film that is mostly claustrophobic waiting and sudden terror, seen from inside a submarine.
Its middle section also puts you on the beach at Dunkirk, inside a novel about guilt rather than a race against time.

h: Two girls vanish in a rainy Pennsylvania town and a father decides the police are too slow; grim, patient and hard to shake.

like.r: Another long, meticulous hunt where obsession eats the investigators, with a real case instead of a fictional one.
Also a suburban child-crime tragedy about fathers and guilt, with an even heavier sense of fate.

like.t: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
like.r: A bleak, procedural-minded hunt for a missing person that works just as well on the page.

h: An idealistic FBI agent is drawn into a shadowy cartel operation along the border; every scene tightens like a vise.

like.r: The same multi-sided look at the drug war, more sprawling and less intent on dread.
Another stark border-country thriller with an unstoppable killer and a world beyond the law's reach.
The sprawling novel of the drug war that shares the film's moral exhaustion and goes decades deeper.

h: A linguist learns an alien language and it changes how she experiences time; first contact told as a story about a mother.

like.t: Stories of Your Life and Others
like.r: The source story sits beside seven others that treat one strange idea each with the same calm rigor.
Another scientist-heroine first contact that cares more about wonder and faith than about invasion.
A slower, stranger meeting with an alien mind that turns into a study of memory and grief.

h: A replicant cop follows a buried secret through orange wastelands and neon ruins; gorgeous, hushed and very long.

like.r: The rain-soaked original it answers, shorter and noirier, with the same question of what makes a person real.

like.t: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
like.r: The novel behind the franchise, stranger and more focused on empathy and fake animals than on action.
An animated cyberpunk meditation on machine selfhood with the same slow, rainy melancholy.

h: The founding of Facebook as a lawsuit-shaped tragedy about friendship, told in dialogue that fires faster than you can follow.

like.r: The great portrait of a self-made titan's loneliness, told in the same patchwork of testimonies.
Another Sorkin script about a brilliant, difficult founder, staged as three backstage confrontations.
The book the film adapts, a breezy, dramatized account of the Harvard feud.

t: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
h: A disgraced journalist and a ferocious hacker dig through a rich family's decades-old disappearance in a frozen Swedish winter.

like.t: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
like.r: The long, procedural novel behind the film, with more of the publishing intrigue and Lisbeth's backstory.
The director's earlier descent into a killer's design, bleaker and more theatrical.
A colder, more procedural obsession with an unsolved case, trading puzzle thrills for exhaustion.

h: A wife disappears and the husband becomes a media villain; a marriage dissected with icy precision and a vicious sense of humor.

like.r: The novel itself, with Flynn writing both the book and the script, so the structure survives but the diary voice is richer.
A pulpier, sexier thriller about a manipulative woman and a man who cannot read her.
Another marriage haunted by a woman who may not be what she seems, wrapped in gothic mood instead of cable news.

h: A young jazz drummer meets a conductor who bullies him toward greatness; scenes of rehearsal play like a fight film.

like.r: Another artist wrecked by perfectionism and a tyrannical teacher, pitched closer to horror.
A music-world rivalry fuelled by envy and genius, grander and far more flamboyant.
The same all-consuming pursuit of excellence at the cost of everything else, in a boxing ring.

h: An actress and a jazz pianist fall in love while chasing careers in Los Angeles; a candy-colored musical with an ache underneath.

like.r: The all-sung French musical that gave the film its bittersweet shape and pastel palette.
The classic Hollywood musical whose joy Chazelle borrows, minus the sad parts.
A smaller, rawer musical romance about two artists whose timing does not quite line up.

h: The Apollo program through Neil Armstrong's private grief, shot with rattling cockpits and a hushed, withdrawn hero.

like.r: The brasher, funnier American space-race epic that First Man deliberately goes quiet against.
A more crowd-pleasing true story of engineers and astronauts under pressure.
Another space film that puts grief and survival in the foreground and makes every hatch feel dangerous.

h: A Sacramento senior fights with her mother, dreams of New York and stumbles through first loves; warm, funny and a little brutal.

like.r: Another growing-up film built from small moments, spread over twelve years instead of one.
Gerwig as co-writer and star in a loose, black-and-white comedy about a young woman drifting through New York.
Another prickly, funny teen girl comedy about a hard bond with a mother and a best friend.

h: The March sisters grow up, quarrel and chase their dreams, with the story folded back on itself so adult regrets color every childhood scene.

like.r: The source novel, plainer and more sermonizing, but with the same four sisters you will already love.
Another costume drama about spirited young women and marriage, with more candlelit yearning.
Gerwig's own contemporary take on a headstrong daughter and a mother who loves her too hard.

h: One man seen at three ages in Miami, learning to hide and then to be touched; hushed, lyrical and quietly devastating.

like.r: Another film that says its love in glances and color, with restraint instead of coming-out.
Also follows one child toward adulthood across years, brighter and more suburban.
A queer love story about shame and desire in the shadow of masculinity, told with the same ache.

h: A young Harlem couple's love is tested when he is jailed for a crime he did not commit; lush, tender and furious.

like.r: The novel behind it, with Baldwin's long, musical sentences carrying the same love and rage.
The director's earlier hushed portrait of Black life and tenderness, more interior and less romantic.
Another Black New York story about injustice, hotter-tempered and more combative.

h: Two twelve-year-olds run off together on a 1965 New England island while the adults panic; storybook, dry and surprisingly moving.

like.r: The director's earlier tale of a precocious misfit and an unlikely crush, more caustic and less fairy-tale.
Lovers on the run in a hushed American landscape, the darker ancestor of this innocent escape.
Another story of a kid running from grown-up phoniness, more angry and less cheerful.

h: A legendary concierge and his lobby boy get dragged into a stolen painting, a prison break and a vanished empire.

like.r: One of the Viennese writers the film openly honors, a gentler and sadder portrait of a vanished Europe.
The director's earlier ensemble comedy of eccentric people, more domestic and less romp.
An elegant old-world comedy of thieves and manners that this film's chatter and sparkle echo.

h: A drifting veteran falls under the sway of a charismatic cult leader in postwar America; strange, magnetic and impossible to pin down.

like.r: The director's other study of a fierce, damaged man and the man who challenges him, more savage and operatic.
Another lonely, volatile ex-soldier adrift in an America that has no place for him.
Postwar drifters chasing a magnetic guru across the country, wilder and less menacing.

h: A stoned Los Angeles private eye chases an ex-girlfriend's trouble through a haze of conspiracies, surfers and one-liners.

like.r: The novel behind the film, even more tangled and silly, with the same warm paranoia.
Another shaggy, stoned detective story where the plot barely matters and the people are everything.
The classic mumbling Los Angeles noir, a loose-limbed ancestor of the same shambling detective.

h: A fastidious couturier in 1950s London falls for a muse who refuses to be managed; a love story as controlled and strange as a fitting.

like.r: Another strange, dangerous marriage in a stately house where control and devotion blur.
A classic of domestic power games between lovers, more melodramatic than this wry, deadpan relationship.
Another period romance of obsession and sensuous restraint.

h: A freed slave and a bounty hunter ride south to rescue his wife; spaghetti-western swagger, bloody jokes and a monstrous Mississippi plantation.

like.t: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly
like.r: The operatic spaghetti western Tarantino keeps borrowing from, colder and quieter.
Another revenge fantasy rewriting history, with Nazis in place of slaveholders.
The same era seen without any genre fun, a harrowing and unflinching true story.

h: Eight strangers wait out a blizzard in a Wyoming haberdashery, and every one of them is lying; talky, mean and gloriously bloody.

like.r: The director's debut, another room of liars and criminals, shorter, leaner and more swaggering.
The paranoid, snowbound whodunit that Tarantino borrowed from, with an alien instead of a poisoner.
A locked-in group of strangers, each with something to hide, being picked off one by one.

t: Once Upon a Time in Hollywood
h: A fading TV cowboy and his stunt double wander through 1969 Los Angeles while history creeps toward them; a shaggy love letter to the city.

like.r: Another sprawling, sunlit ensemble about a subculture of the movie business and its fall.
The dark classic about Hollywood leaving its stars behind, sharper and much more bitter.
The director's own loose ensemble, with all the chatter but a tighter, nastier pace.

h: A U.S. marshal investigates a missing patient at a storm-bound asylum island, and the fog thickens into something personal.

like.r: The novel behind it, with the dread built more slowly and the final turn hitting harder on the page.
Another film that makes you doubt the detective's reality, trading gothic mood for a puzzle.
The classic obsessive-investigator mystery whose spiral of delusion this film echoes.

h: A stockbroker builds a boiler-room empire on fraud, drugs and charisma; three hours of manic excess that never tells you to stop laughing.

like.r: The director's earlier rise-and-fall narrated by an addict of the lifestyle, with mobsters instead of stockbrokers.
A far darker satire of money-drunk New York, with ice where this one has cocaine.
The great satirical novel of ambitious bond traders and their downfall.

h: A hitman looks back on decades in the mob and his friendship with Jimmy Hoffa; an elegiac, three-and-a-half-hour reckoning with violence and age.

like.r: The towering mob saga that also tracks decades of loyalty, with more operatic grandeur.

like.t: Once Upon a Time in America
like.r: Another long, melancholy look back at gangster friendship and betrayal.
The younger, faster and more exuberant counterpart, where this one is its sad, old-age answer.

h: An orphan hidden in a Paris train station's clockwork finds a toymaker with a lost past; Scorsese's love letter to early cinema.

like.r: The illustrated novel it adapts, half in pictures, with the same mystery and the same love of automata.
Another valentine to old-time movie magic, more bittersweet and set in a small Italian town.
A Paris fairy tale with the same clockwork whimsy, aimed at grown-ups and romance.

h: A stubborn fourteen-year-old hires a drunken marshal to track her father's killer; formal talk, dry laughs and a tough little heroine.

like.r: The novel behind both films, narrated in Mattie's priggish, hilarious voice.
A bleaker, more somber western about an old gunman and the cost of reputation.
The same directors in darker mode, with a pursuit across Texas and far less warmth.

h: A talented, difficult folk singer spends a freezing week in 1961 Greenwich Village going nowhere; funny, gray and deeply sad.

like.r: Another Coen portrait of a man worn down by an indifferent universe, steeped in Jewish suburban absurdism.
A warmer film about a struggling street musician, hopeful where this one is cold.

like.t: Dave Van Ronk: The Mayor of MacDougal Street
like.r: The folk singer's own memoir, the real Village scene that the film's hero stumbles through.

h: A studio fixer in 1951 Hollywood juggles a kidnapped star, a gossip twin and a chorus of musical numbers in one frantic day.

like.r: The classic comedy about Hollywood's relationship to real life, sunnier and more sentimental.
The Coens' darker, weirder take on the studio system, a nightmare instead of a farce.
The musical comedy about the studio era that this one parodies and adores.

h: Six Western tales, from a singing gunslinger to a stagecoach of strangers, each a different joke about death.

like.r: Another deadpan, strange western that treats the frontier as a place of drifting toward death.
Another film of linked tales with a mean sense of humor, in a modern setting.
The darkest literary western, with violence that is not played for laughs.

h: After a botched robbery, a desperate Queens hustler spends one neon night trying to spring his brother; relentless and sweaty.

like.r: Another New York robbery gone wrong, with an ordinary desperate man at its center.
The scrappy, street-level ancestor, about a small-time crook and the brother he cannot save.
Another synth-lit night-crime movie, cooler and more romantic than this panic attack.

h: A Diamond District jeweler bets everything on one more score, and two hours of shouting makes your pulse hammer.

like.r: A classic of the self-destructive gambler, with a cooler and more literary despair.
Another study of gambling as appetite, with the mob providing the stakes.
Another night-city film following an obsessed hustler who cannot stop pushing his luck.

h: Two women scheme for the affection of a sickly, volatile Queen Anne; a poisonous palace comedy shot through fisheye lenses.

like.r: Another candlelit eighteenth-century world of ambition and cruelty, colder and more austere.
Another elegant court of manipulators, with seduction as their weapon of choice.
A sharp novel of Tudor power and survival, with the same knowing eye for court politics.

h: Single people must find a partner at a hotel in forty-five days or be turned into an animal; deadpan, cruel and oddly romantic.

like.r: A quiet dystopia in which people accept an absurd system without complaint, sadder and less comic.

like.t: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
like.r: Another strange-premise romance about whether love can be engineered, warmer and messier.
Another dystopia where the state polices intimacy, with fury instead of deadpan.

t: The Killing of a Sacred Deer
h: A surgeon is pursued by a polite teenager who says his family must pay for an old mistake; flat voices and mounting dread.

like.r: Another cold study of a family under the control of polite intruders, even more punishing.
The director's earlier, even stranger film about a family with its own rules.
Another cold, stylized morality play in which a community turns on one person and cruelty is rendered with deadpan formality.

h: A broke, unfinished dancer in her late twenties bounces between apartments in New York as her best friend drifts away; funny and tender.

like.r: Another black-and-white love letter to New York, with neurotic charm and a very different protagonist.
Gerwig's solo follow-up, a warmer and more structured look at ambition and home.
Another neurotic New York comedy about a relationship and a woman who refuses to be defined by it.

h: A theater director and an actress try to divorce kindly and find the legal system turning them against each other; funny, then crushing.

like.r: The classic custody-battle drama that this film updates, with a more even-handed look at both sides.
The great unflinching dissection of a marriage ending, colder and more philosophical.
Another film that cuts between a marriage's start and its collapse, rawer and more bleak.

h: Filmed over twelve years with the same cast, a Texas boy grows up in front of you through small, ordinary scenes.

like.r: The director's earlier film of time passing between two people, compressed into a single night.
The great childhood film about a boy failing to fit in, harsher and more personal.
A play that also finds its poetry in the plain moments of ordinary lives.

h: Celine and Jesse, nine years after the last time, talk through a Greek holiday that turns into a fight about their whole life together.

like.r: Where the couple began: a night of walking and talking in Vienna, breezier and full of possibility.
Another talky relationship comedy that looks honestly at how love wears down.
A far more bitter portrait of a marriage coming apart, with fewer jokes.

h: A college baseball team's last weekend before classes in 1980: parties, pranks and big talk by guys on the verge of adulthood.

like.r: The spiritual predecessor from the same director, set in 1976 high school, a little rawer.
The classic one-night coming-of-age comedy with a jukebox soundtrack and a similar warm haze.
Ruder, crazier campus comedy with a very similar flavor of male friendship.

h: A free Black violinist is kidnapped and sold into slavery in Louisiana; an unflinching true story that does not look away.

like.r: The great novel of slavery's aftermath, more lyrical and ghostly, equally hard to read.
The memoir on which the film is based, first-hand and plain-spoken.
Another historical atrocity film shot with a stark eye, ending in some hope.

h: A polished New Yorker's compulsive private life unravels when his messy sister moves in; cold, explicit and sad.

like.r: Another lonely man in the city whose isolation hardens into something frightening.
A frantic portrait of addiction, louder and more hallucinatory than this chilly one.
The director's debut, another unblinking study of a body pushed to its limit.

h: A has-been superhero actor stages a Broadway play in what looks like one unbroken take, with his ego and his past shouting at him.

like.r: Another dazzling portrait of an artist burning himself down for a show.
Another art-making film where the performer's mind frays on opening night.
A scorching satire of media fame and breakdown, angrier and talkier.

h: A frontiersman left for dead crawls across a frozen wilderness for revenge; an endurance test shot in natural light.

like.r: Another obsessive journey into a hostile landscape, stranger and more fevered.
A smaller-scale survival tale of one person against the wild, for a younger audience.
A man-against-nature survival movie in the snow, with wolves and a lot of grief.

h: A medical engineer is stranded in orbit after debris wrecks her shuttle; ninety minutes of weightless, near-silent panic.

like.r: A true story of astronauts stranded in space, less introspective, more engineers solving problems.
The visual ancestor of every silent, floating shot, colder and cosmic.
Another one-person survival film, at sea instead of in orbit.

h: A one-armed warrior and a drifter race a war rig across the desert; two hours of practical chases, painted war boys and fury.

like.r: The earlier film that defined the wasteland chase, raw, leaner and with less spectacle.
Another action classic that makes a tough woman its center, in space instead of on the road.
The quiet, bleak counterpart: the post-apocalypse as a father's walk, not a chase.

h: A young coder is brought to a remote lab to test whether a humanoid robot can think; three people, one house, and everyone is lying.

like.r: The classic about what makes an artificial being a person, grander and noir.
Linked stories that probe the ethics of thinking machines, more puzzle than menace.
Another AI-and-human story, with tenderness where this one has a trap.

h: A biologist joins an expedition into a shimmering zone where nature is rewriting itself; beautiful, unnerving and open to interpretation.

like.r: The novel behind it, stranger, quieter and more ambiguous than Garland's film.
The great expedition into a forbidden zone, slower and more philosophical.
Another hypnotic and alien film that turns human identity strange.

h: A hit man whose targets are sent back from the future must kill his own older self; a time-travel thriller with a surprising heart.

like.r: The time-travel classic in a friendlier key, with the same fascination for paradox.
Another bleak time-travel puzzle where the past cannot be changed.
The original hunter-from-the-future chase thriller, lean and relentless.

h: A famous mystery novelist dies at his birthday party and a Southern detective picks through a family of liars; a modern Agatha Christie.

like.r: The model for the closed-circle whodunit, bleaker and without the sly social satire.
A sillier, more slapstick take on the same house-full-of-suspects game.
Another murder at a country house that is equally about the class divide upstairs and downstairs.

h: The Resistance runs from a relentless fleet while Rey seeks answers from a bitter Luke Skywalker; a divisive, big-hearted blockbuster.

like.r: The darker middle chapter it openly echoes, with its own heroes in retreat.
A different grand space saga, more austere and religious.
The novel behind much of the genre's politics and prophecy, denser and slower.

h: A slacker bassist must defeat his new girlfriend's seven evil exes in video-game duels; a comic-book rom-com with every frame in motion.

like.r: The graphic novel the film compresses, softer and slower with more room for the characters.
Another hyperactive comic adaptation with a young-adult swagger, much more violent.
A direct-to-camera charmer for slackers, in a gentler suburb.

h: Five middle-aged friends reunite to finish a twelve-pub crawl and stumble into an alien takeover; a laugh-out-loud farce with a sad heart.

like.r: The same team's earlier take, a zombie comedy with a lighter and sweeter view of friendship.
Another British genre parody built on bromance and a quiet village hiding a nasty secret.
The paranoid classic about replaced neighbors that this film cheerfully pastiches.

h: A getaway driver who needs music to concentrate tries to leave crime behind; each car chase is choreographed to its song.

like.r: Another silent getaway driver with a romance, colder and much more violent.
A music-and-mayhem road comedy, goofier and looser.
The crime epic whose crews and heists inform the genre, darker and more sprawling.

h: A defiant foster kid and his gruff guardian flee into the New Zealand bush with the whole country chasing them.

like.r: The director's earlier, quieter New Zealand story of a kid and an absent father.
Another warm, deadpan comedy about an outsider finding a family.
The original novel, rougher and drier, with the same bush-and-banter pairing.

h: A lonely boy in the Hitler Youth, with an imaginary Hitler for a friend, discovers a girl hiding in his attic; a satire that turns sincere.

like.r: Another film that uses comedy and a child's perspective to look at the Second World War, more tender.
The original comedy that mocks Hitler to his face, broader and earlier.
Another story of a child growing up in wartime Germany, more lyrical and unapologetically sad.

h: A stranded Thor fights gladiator battles with the Hulk before facing his sister on Asgard; Marvel at its loosest, funniest and most colorful.

like.r: Another jokey, neon-soaked Marvel space romp with a found-family heart.
The campy space adventure whose gaudy costumes and Queen soundtrack this film often echoes.
Another action-comedy in which a swaggering hero is out of his depth and everyone around him is funnier.

h: A six-year-old runs wild through a pastel motel near Disney World while her mother scrapes by; joyful and heartbreaking at once.

like.r: The model of the humane, poor-street realist drama, centered on a father and son.
Another bright, messy portrait of young people living on the edge of the American economy.
Another Florida story of a child growing up poor, quieter and more lyrical.

h: Two trans sex workers cross Los Angeles on Christmas Eve hunting for a cheating boyfriend; a shot-on-iPhone comedy that crackles.

like.r: A classic of two outcast friends hustling in a hard city, moodier and sadder.
Another single-day, street-level film that mixes comedy and fury in a loud neighborhood.
The documentary of New York's queer ball culture, with similar fierce chosen families.

h: A withdrawn janitor returns to his Massachusetts hometown to care for his teenage nephew and face what he left behind; funny in places, devastating.

like.r: Another quiet New England film in which grief wears down a family.
The classic drama of a family unable to speak about a death.
A longer, much more punishing novel about trauma and the friends who try to carry a man through it.

h: A family hides a grandmother's terminal diagnosis and stages a wedding as an excuse to say goodbye; wry, warm and full of food.

like.r: Another comedy of family pressure across cultures, more farcical and equally heartfelt.
Another gentle immigrant-family story told through grandparents and kids.
A novel of Chinese mothers and American daughters trying to understand each other across a cultural gap.

h: Kayla's final week of middle school is a series of excruciating, hilarious attempts to be seen, filmed with an anxious pulse.

like.r: A teen comedy about a girl and her mother, a little older and more sheltered.
A sharper, wittier take on a teenage girl's rough year.

like.t: Are You There God? It's Me, Margaret.
like.r: The classic book of girls and awkward growing up, gentler and set in an earlier time.

h: Two overachieving best friends try to cram four years of partying into one graduation-eve night; raunchy, quick and full of love.

like.r: The boys' version of this one-crazy-night comedy, cruder with an equally big friendship at its core.
Another sharp, female-led high school comedy with a wit of its own.
The quotable high-school comedy classic, more about cliques than friendship.

h: Six mismatched heroes bicker, then fight an alien army over Manhattan; the first big superhero crossover, built on banter.

like.r: The classic team-of-misfits mission movie, grittier and more cynical.
A funnier, family-sized superhero ensemble with a sharp sense of fun.
The blockbuster adventure that taught audiences to love a band of unlikely allies.

h: Every Marvel hero converges to stop a cosmic warlord collecting six stones; huge, crowded and unexpectedly bleak.

like.t: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King
like.r: The model of the multi-front epic with a world on the line, more earnest and mythic.
The funnier, scrappier cosmic team-up that sets up the same threat.
The original blockbuster in which the heroes lose, a smaller and more personal take.

h: Marvel's surviving heroes try to undo a catastrophe over three hours that pay off a decade of films; an emotional victory lap.

like.r: The model of the fun, rule-bound time-travel caper, brighter and much simpler.

like.t: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King
like.r: Another long, tear-stained finale for a big cast, with kings and hobbits in place of Avengers.
A smaller, grittier time-travel story that also cares more about what it costs than how it works.

h: A young king returns to hidden Wakanda to find his throne challenged by a cousin with a vengeful point; Marvel with real political teeth.

like.r: The royal-succession story with a vengeful relative that this film often calls to mind, with songs and lions.
The director's earlier crowd-pleaser, a smaller and more intimate drama of legacy.
A short Afrofuturist novella set among bright African tech and old traditions.

h: A cocky space thief and four misfits fight over a mysterious orb to a soundtrack of 1970s hits; Marvel at its most cheerful.

like.r: The adventure that this film openly loves, with its own band of rogues and a similar sense of fun.
Another ragtag space crew with banter and heart, drier and more western.

like.t: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
like.r: The funniest space comedy on the shelf, sillier and wordier.

h: A hero from the forties finds his own agency rotten in a Marvel version of a 1970s paranoid thriller.

like.r: The paranoid spy thriller that inspired this film, leaner and cynical.
Another trained operative fighting the institution that made him, with grounded fights and chases.
Another older, institution-testing spy story that likes its old-fashioned hero.

h: An Amazon princess leaves her island to end the First World War and discovers that people are not so easily sorted into good and evil.

like.r: A similar old-fashioned war-era superhero film with a sincere heart.
The classic uplifting hero story about an outsider with great power, sweeter and more mythic.
Another film about a fierce woman at its center, in a far wilder and more violent register.

h: A failed clown in a decaying Gotham is pushed into violence; a grim, slow character study with a hypnotic performance at its center.

like.r: The lonely, deteriorating man in a filthy city that this film models itself on, with deeper grit.
A different delusional would-be comedian chasing fame, darker comedy and a colder world.
Another sociopathic outsider rising in a rotten city, more satirical and fast.

h: An old, worn-out Wolverine drives a dying Professor X and a mysterious child to the border; a superhero western about the cost of violence.

like.r: The classic western that this film quotes, about a gunman who cannot escape his reputation.
The late western about an old killer and the price of the violence that he is known for.
Another bleak road-movie escort of a miraculous child through a collapsing near-future.

h: A New York professor meets her boyfriend's fabulously rich Singapore family; a lavish, bright comedy about love, money and a terrifying future mother-in-law.

like.r: The satirical novel behind the film, even more gossipy and over the top, with footnotes.
Another comedy of a woman facing her partner's close-knit and overbearing family.
Another glamorous fairy tale about love across a class divide.

h: A man fresh out of a psychiatric hospital and a grieving widow agree to enter a dance contest; a shouty, warm romance about damaged people.

like.r: Another romantic comedy about a difficult, obsessive man and the woman who tolerates him.
The novel behind the film, first-person and more rambling, with the same hope and the same Eagles obsession.

like.t: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
like.r: Another offbeat romance between two bruised people, stranger and more melancholy.

h: A broke maid of honor sabotages herself and a friend's wedding build-up; gross-out set pieces and a big, bruised heart.

like.r: Another wedding-weekend disaster comedy, with the boys in place of the bridesmaids.
Another sharp comedy of female friendship and rivalry, at school.
A more polished wedding comedy about a woman who cannot bear a friend's happiness.

h: A whip-smart high-school girl lets a rumor of promiscuity grow into a fully grown reputation; a sassy riff on The Scarlet Letter.

like.r: The novel whose branded heroine the film cheerfully parodies, with real stakes.
Another sparkling classic teen comedy rebuilt from a literary source.
Another quotable comedy about reputation, school and who gets to tell your story.

h: A Pakistani-American comic's girlfriend falls into a coma and he bonds with her parents; a true story that moves between funny and frightened.
